It’s better to keep your mouth shut and appear stupid than to open it and remove all doubt,” my daughter Monica said, quoting a phrase often attributed to Mark Twain, as we stepped into the great novelist’s wonderfully eccentric Connecticut home on the second day of our father-daughter road trip through New England.

We had collected a black Subaru Forester from JFK airport and set off on an unusual 2,000-mile pilgrimage through the literary heart of New England. The idea was simple enough: visit the homes of America’s greatest writers, trace the landscapes that shaped them, and see whether genius leaves any trace in the places it once inhabited. It also doubled as a search for good food and long, uninterrupted conversations on the open road.

Mark Twain’s Hartford house is unlike any literary shrine. It looks as though a Mississippi steamboat has collided with a Victorian Gothic mansion and then been left to settle into something exuberantly American. Red brick, ornate chimneys and playful gables give it the air of a building that refuses to take itself too seriously.

open image in gallery Mark Twain’s house is defined by its red brick, ornate chimneys and playful gables ( Adams & Knight )

Inside, the guide referred to him exclusively as “Sam”, as though Samuel Clemens had simply stepped out for a moment. Monica happily discussed Huckleberry Finn while I quietly realised how much I had forgotten. Parents are supposed to know more than their children. Literary pilgrimages have a way of correcting such assumptions.

The house, built with the fortune of Twain’s heiress wife Olivia, was one of the first in America to have electricity and central heating. In 1881 they commissioned Louis Comfort Tiffany to transform the interiors into a theatrical blaze of embossed wallpaper, stencilled ceilings and deep reds and golds. It was spectacularly expensive and eventually helped drive Twain back onto the lecture circuit to repair the family finances.

Just a short walk away stands the more modest home of Harriet Beecher Stowe, author of Uncle Tom’s Cabin. It is hard to imagine a more concentrated patch of American literary history. In the billiard room upstairs, Twain wrote much of Huckleberry Finn, the novel often described as the foundation of modern American literature. Standing there, it was impossible not to see his journey – from riverboat pilot and penniless journalist to national figure – as a version of the American dream itself.

That first stop set the tone for everything that followed.

Over the next fortnight we crossed much of New England, tracing the lives of Herman Melville, Emily Dickinson, Louisa May Alcott, Edith Wharton, and the transcendentalists Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau. Between them came bass fishing, canoeing, long glacial lakes, strawberry fields, village greens and white-steepled churches. And everywhere, inevitably, lobster rolls and clam chowder.

The journey had been inspired partly by cinema. Paper Moon and On Golden Pond had long suggested that travel matters as much as arrival. (Fans of On Golden Pond should stay at the Von Horn Estate, which is a country house hotel actually on the lake.) Our version was considerably calmer. The only recurring dispute was musical. I leaned towards Pink Floyd; Monica introduced Geese, whom she described as “the modern Bob Dylan”. We found as much agreement over books as playlists as we juggled from the Grateful Dead to Oasis.

open image in gallery Long hours in the car created a space for family conversations that ordinary life rarely allows ( The Independent )

As the miles accumulated, something subtle shifted. Long hours in the car created a space for conversation that ordinary life rarely allows. Books gave way to politics, music, careers and the strange pleasure of simply observing America unfold beyond the windscreen. New England itself became part of the dialogue: maple forests blazing green, empty highways, and towns where white clapboard houses still gathered around village greens as though time had paused.

New England contains both astonishing beauty and an extraordinary density of history. Here, the first shots of the American Revolution were fired. Here, a young nation began to imagine itself. Here, writers would later find the landscapes that defined its literature. We stayed in a treehouse at The Winvian, a Connecticut country estate with 18 cottages that offers seasonal delicacies in its restaurant. There were warnings to look out for wild bears, but the more obvious reality was the charming bike rides in the nearby woods. Hotels are part of the American dream.

By the time we left Hartford, the purpose of the journey had already begun to shift. We had set out in search of writers’ houses. What we were discovering instead was something less tangible but more enduring: the pleasure of uninterrupted time together, measured in miles rather than minutes.

open image in gallery The treehouse accommodation at at The Winvian in Connecticut ( The Independent )



In the Berkshires, Herman Melville’s house at Arrowhead sits quietly beneath the shadow of Mount Greylock. It is modest, almost understated, and all the more powerful for it. Here, Moby-Dick was written – an epic that failed on publication and would not find its audience for decades.

Looking out across the landscape, it was easy to imagine Melville wrestling with his creation while the world outside remained indifferent. Every literary house seemed to carry the same lesson: recognition and talent rarely arrive at the same time. A wonderful diversion from the driver’s seat was staying at Prospect Berkshires on a lake with super-stylish cabins and sauna huts, a zeitgeisty resort that leans into its stunning waterscape.

In Amherst, Emily Dickinson’s house offers a different kind of intensity. Small rooms, restrained light and a life deliberately narrowed to allow imagination to expand. She published almost nothing in her lifetime, yet her poetry now feels foundational to modern literature.

open image in gallery Emily Dickinson’s house has small rooms and restrained light ( Lynne Graves Photography )

A short drive away, Louisa May Alcott’s Orchard House tells another story entirely – one of family, imagination and quiet radicalism. Little Women was written here, drawing directly on domestic life yet reshaping it into something far more enduring. If Dickinson represents solitude, Alcott represents connection.

At Concord, Emerson and Thoreau’s world feels more conceptual than domestic. Walden Pond, in particular, where Thoreau lived in a wood hut for two years, two months and two days, resists cliché. It is smaller than expected, quieter, more ordinary – and yet it remains one of the most influential landscapes in American thought.

Here, nature was not scenery but philosophy. Simplicity was not aesthetic but moral. Walking the shoreline, it was easy to see how a new relationship between people and the natural world was once imagined here.

Between these lit-stops, New England revealed itself in less formal ways. Diners with creaking porches served eggs, hash browns and endless coffee. Coastal towns offered lobster rolls eaten at picnic tables overlooking grey Atlantic water. Lakes stretched long and still beneath impossible skies.

open image in gallery New England revealed itself to be at the forefront of Americana ( The Independent )

Standouts in New Haven, Connecticut, were sessional family pizza restaurant Modern Apizza and an oceanside seafood restaurant, Shell and Bones, that has true piquancy and zest for utterly delicious seafood. Do not pass on the oysters. Another stunning food high-spot was Woods Hill Table, a perfect local restaurant in Lexington, Massachusetts, with a sophisticated vibe.

New England has always been, we reminded ourselves, at the forefront of Americana: Jaws, The Stepford Wives, Nathaniel Hawthorne’s The Scarlet Letter and Arlo Guthrie’s plaintive anti-Vietnam tour de force “Alice’s Restaurant”.

At Lexington, Massachusetts, history becomes physical. On the village green where the first shots of the American Revolution were fired, Gerry Marrocco, a charismatic guide in period costume, recounted Paul Revere’s midnight ride, warning “the Brits are coming” with evangelical precision. It is easy to forget how recent this history is.

open image in gallery Guide Gerry Marrocco recounts Paul Revere’s midnight ride ( The Independent )

We stayed at the Inn at Hastings Park in Lexington, Massachusetts, which has been converted by its perfectionist owner Trisha Kennealy to be a beacon of high American cuisine. It is on the old Boston coach road and worth any diversion.

Nearby architecture tells a different story of reinvention. The Bauhaus-inspired house designed by Walter Gropius in Massachusetts feels like a clean break from the past – precise, modern, almost radical in its simplicity. New England is rarely one thing for long. Gropius’s house is enchanting and revolutionary.

Somewhere along these roads, another journey was taking place.

Monica and I shared driving, music and long stretches of silence punctuated by argument and laughter. We disagreed over playlists, agreed over food, and slowly accumulated a shared map of references that belonged only to us.

The landscape itself seemed to encourage it. Maple-lined roads, sudden glimpses of lake, and towns with names that echoed American history – Concord, Salem, Lexington, New Haven – created a rhythm that made conversation inevitable. New ventures reflect the entrepreneurial as well as the indulgent.

The Lake Estate on Winnisquam is a £100m dream vacation spot created by Patti and Ed Rocco. It’s straight out of a Robert Redford idyll, arcadian and ambitious. It seems to whisper from their side of the pond: eat your heart out, Lake Como. What began as a literary pilgrimage had become something else, a reminder that time together is not an incidental benefit of travel, but its real purpose.

open image in gallery The beautiful Lake Estate on Winnisquam ( The Lake Estate on Winnisquam )

By the end of 2,000 miles, we had visited writers who shaped a nation’s imagination and landscapes that shaped theirs. But the most lasting impression was not literary at all. It was the sense that journeys rarely deliver what they promise – and often deliver something better instead.

We set out to understand America through its greatest writers. We ended up understanding something simpler: that travel changes not only what you see, but how you talk to the person beside you. Twain believed that travel is fatal to prejudice. He might also have added that it is remarkably good for families.

How to do it

Journeyscape offers a 14-day Classic New England package, including visits to Boston, Plymouth, Cape Cod and the islands, Acadia National Park, the Berkshires, New Hampshire Lakes, Connecticut, Woodstock, Portland and more. From £4,180pp per person, excluding flights.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

News.title: Britain to pay higher Trump tariffs than EU
News.content:
Britain will pay higher tariffs than the EU after Donald Trump’s latest global trade onslaught.

Bosses in Britain have warned they will lose any competitive advantage over the bloc after the US President announced higher import taxes on goods from 60 trading partners.

The US administration imposed 10pc tariffs on both Britain and the EU to replace levies which expired overnight following a Supreme Court ruling earlier this year.

Britain must pay the import taxes on top of so-called Most Favoured Nation tariffs imposed on all members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

However, from Friday, the EU’s tariffs are inclusive of the WTO levies. The average WTO tariff rate is between 2.4pc to 3.5pc for non-agricultural food products.

William Bain, head of trade policy at the BCC, said: “There will be concerns about the loss of the UK’s competitive advantage over the EU and other countries which have secured a more favourable deal in other goods sectors.”

A government spokesman said: “There is no negative ‌change ‌to ⁠the tariff rate facing UK businesses as a result of this ⁠announcement.”

“Our agreement with the US remains in place, and today we see ​an improvement to our ‌trading terms with zero tariffs on whisky and medical technology.”

Jonathan Reynolds, the Business Secretary, said Scottish whisky distilleries would get a “boost” from the new tariff regime, which removes levies on scotch under a deal first announced during the King’s state visit to the US in April.

On Friday, Trump also threatened new tariffs on the European Union in response to billions worth of fines imposed on US tech giants by competition regulators.

In a post on his social media platform Truth Social, Trump said: “The United States of America is not a “PIGGYBANK” for Europe, nor will we allow it to be!”

The US president said he expected to impose “substantial tariffs” on the EU after the European Commission fined Google €890m (£760m) on Thursday.

UK and European stock markets shrugged off the latest tariffs, with the FTSE 100 up 0.9pc.

However, Wall Street was more mixed. The S&P 500 was roughly flat, while the Nasdaq Composite was down 1.1pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.3pc near the end of Friday’s trading session.

It followed dramatic falls in Asia overnight, with Japan’s Nikkei falling 2.7pc and South Korea’s Kospi down 5.7pc.

News.title: Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs
News.content:
It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

News.title: Eleanor Cardwell: ‘Comfortable sportswear should not be expensive’
News.content:
What sports shoes do you recommend?

Robert, South West

The sports shoes that I’m currently wearing are from Puma. They’re very comfortable and have support. I actually wear a basketball shoe at the minute to have more support up the ankle.

A lot of the girls wear Asics as well, which I know is the netball shoe. I’ve worn Puma for the last four years, so I would recommend them.

But honestly, whatever works best for you, you have to try them out. Whatever is best for your instep and whatever is comfiest. And if you need more ankle support, you can put some ankle braces on.

How has playing for Manchester Thunder helped you develop as a player?

Jason, London

Manchester has massively helped me develop as a player. I’ve been playing here since 2012. As a young girl, it created me as a person, to be honest with you. It’s such a family environment that I think a lot of my values come from this club. So my family values, being connected, creating energy – all those things come rooted from this club, which is incredible.

I think whatever step you are in your career, whether you’re a young athlete or senior, they help you develop. Even now I’m 31, they’re still helping me learn new things on the court. The coaches are incredible, and I’m constantly learning and being inspired by them every single week.

Do players retire from elite netball quite young?

Helen, South West

I think it depends on the athlete. Some can retire at 40, and that’s because their bodies are so conditioned, and they might not have had any major injuries in their career. They’re able to continue to push themselves all the way until 40.

But I’d say the average is probably mid-30s. Now the Super League has become professional, the younger athletes are getting better training from a younger age. We want to keep pushing ourselves to play as long as possible.

How can netball get more coverage when women’s football is constantly pushed?

Sarah, South West

I think netball needs to have more sponsors to get more media coverage. Bigger sponsors.

Players need to put their personalities more out there on social media, so brands will want to work with us. Everyone’s got amazing personalities in netball. They [brands] should want to be a part of the netball players’ stories and the netball teams.

But it’s about getting as much exposure as possible, and making sure that everyone is going on YouTube or BBC, so more people are able to learn about the sport.

I loved netball at school. How do I get involved now in my 60s?

Sue, Yorkshire

Netball is for everyone. I personally love going to walking netball sessions and taking them through classes. You can go to the England Netball website and find out where you can play locally.

There’s also Back to Netball, depending on your ability and what you want to get out of it. Personally, I think walking netball is so much fun. The women who are in those sessions are a huge laugh, and I know when I retire, I’m going to be joining a group, for sure.

Apart from netball, what other hobbies do you have? How do they help you relieve the pressure of competition?

George, London

I feel like over the past few years I’ve really got into some new hobbies. I love reading. I love fantasy reading, like Throne of Glass. I love BookTok, so I’ve really got into that.

I’m also very crafty. I like making things – I’ve made little crochet bees for all the girls, and I like drawing, and painting occasionally – just wholesome activities to take me away from netball life. As soon as I zone in on an activity, I’m locked in and I have to complete it.

News.title: Africa improves health defences, but it remains vulnerable to pandemics
News.content:
Africa is significantly better prepared for a pandemic than it was five years ago, a major review of the continent’s health security has found.

The review, which tracked dozens of health metrics across the continent, found that local and international investments in Africa’s health sector since the pandemic have “paid off.”

Published by the Brown University Pandemic Centre and the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a US non-profit, the report is the third of its kind and provides an update on two previous reviews from 2019 and 2021.

Investment in health by African governments grew rapidly during the pandemic. Post-pandemic, the average spend now sits at around 7.4 per cent of GDP, roughly $135 billion per year across the continent.

That figure still falls significantly below those of high-income countries, where the average spend on health sits at around 11.2 per cent of GDP.

The new African Health Security Index report found that almost every African country – 53 out of 54, excluding only the Republic of the Congo – has improved its ability to prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks since 2021, the last time the index was updated.

Overall, the continent scores 41.2 out of 100 on its health security – up from 32.9 five years ago.

The score is built from hundreds of specific indicators covering things like how far people live from a hospital, how well infectious patients can be isolated, the size and training level of the health workforce, laboratory capacity, and the availability of vaccines and other critical medicines during an outbreak.

Sports.title: Barcelona release statement as construction worker tragically dies during Nou Camp stadium renovation
Sports.content:
BARCELONA have released a statement after a construction worker died on the site of the Camp Nou.

The iconic stadium is still undergoing renovations which began in 2023.



The Blaugrana’s statement said: “FC Barcelona deeply regrets the death of the worker who lost his life yesterday in the workplace accident that occurred during the renovation works at Spotify Camp Nou.

“The Club wishes to express its deepest condolences and extend its heartfelt support to his family, friends, and colleagues.



“FC Barcelona President Joan Laporta wishes to personally convey his condolences to the family and places himself at their disposal on behalf of the entire Club.”

The accident came during Barca’s renovation work, which is now in its third year.

The Catalan giants returned to the stadium with a reduced capacity last term.

However, recent reports suggest the club might have to temporarily wave goodbye to their famous old ground once again next year.

The Spanish champions have reportedly asked Barcelona City Council for permission to use the Estadi Olimpic Lluis Companys – known as the Montjuïc – during the first half of the 2027/28 season.

Barcelona spent two seasons playing at the Montjuïc between 2023/24 and 2024/25, and at the start of this season they fluctuated between there and their training ground – the Johan Cruyff Stadium – before moving back into the Camp Nou in November.



One of the most complicated stages of the renovation project is scheduled to begin in the summer of 2027.

That phase involves installing the new roof structure over the stadium.

As a result, Barcelona fear they may not be able to host matches at the Camp Nou during the opening months of the 2027/28 campaign.

The proposed roof is set to become one of the standout features of the revamped stadium.

For now, plans are in place to increase the capacity bit by bit, with 80,000 fans expected later this year.



There could be a full crowd of 105,000 by April 2027.

Sports.title: Top 10 biggest Premier League transfers ever at today’s prices with Cristiano Ronaldo worth nearly £300m
Sports.content:
THE Premier League’s biggest ever sales, adjusted for inflation, have been revealed.

This summer has so far seen three Premier League players sold for £100million or more, those being Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali.



However, none of those deals even come close to the all-time biggest deals list once they are adjusted for inflation.

The figures of those deals have been calculated by Valuball.



And it is Cristiano Ronaldo‘s first Manchester United exit to Real Madrid in 2009 which takes the top spot by some margin.

The deal to take the then reigning Ballon d’Or winner from Old Trafford to the Bernabeu cost £80million at the time.



But the deal would now be worth a staggering £292m, making it almost three times the value of the deal that took Tonali to Tottenham from Newcastle.

A more modern deal is ranked in second place, with Eden Hazard‘s transfer from Chelsea to Real Madrid in 2019 now being worth £245m.

It was a deal that saw £150m paid in total after performance related bonuses were met by trophy wins, despite Hazard failing to live up to the hype with a wave of injuries that defined his Real career.

Taking third is the first all English club transfer on the list with Alan Shearer‘s move from Blackburn to Newcastle.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

In 1996 it was a £15m deal, but today it would cost a whopping £238m.

La Liga giants Real swoop in once again with the fourth largest deal ever thanks to their 1999 purchase of Nicolas Anelka from Arsenal costing £23.5m at the time.

Now a deal for the Frenchman would cost a staggering £226m.

Another England to Spain flop proved to be Philippe Coutinho‘s switch from Liverpool to Barcelona.



That 2017 move – which funded Jurgen Klopp‘s spine that would go on to win the Prem and Champions League for the Reds – was still a sizeable £142m at the time, but would now be worth £217m.

Paul Gascoigne‘s sale from Tottenham to Italian giants Lazio makes it to sixth on the list, with the £5.5m move in 1992 adjusted to be valued at £197m today.

Arsenal sold another big hitter in Marc Overmars to Real Madrid in 2000 for £25m, and that deal would now be an incredible £196m – meaning the Gunners would have pocketed more than £400m in sales from Real across two summers.

Gareth Bale was another player to move from North London to Spain, and proved to be the best of that selection.



The Welshman moved from Spurs to Real for £86m in 2013, and that deal would now be worth £192m.

Rounding out the top 10 are deals that took Stan Collymore from Nottingham Forest to Liverpool and Rio Ferdinand from Leeds to Man Utd.

Collymore’s 1995 deal would shatter the record sale Forest got for Anderson as they sold him to Manchester City for £116m, with the former English transfer record of £8.5m costing £179m if it were done today.

Meanwhile, Ferdinand’s deal to go from Elland Road to Old Trafford in 2002 was also a British record at £30m.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But today the deal for the English defender would be an eye-watering £175m.

The actual record deal is Alexander Isak’s switch from Newcastle to Liverpool last summer for £130m, but even that figure only puts it at 24th most valuable when adjusted for inflation.

Sports.title: Why Maxence Lacroix is the key to Xabi Alonso’s 3-4-3 tactical revolution at Chelsea after Crystal Palace move
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO wanted a leader and Chelsea have gone out and got him a pastor.

The France defender, 26, has agreed a six-year deal to join the Blues from London rivals Crystal Palace and relishes his role as a leader.



Oliver Glasner signed the defender for Crystal Palace from Wolfsburg, having worked with Lacroix at the German club.

Lacroix has a fierce sense of fun but is also deeply religious, and called himself ‘the pastor’ after joining Palace, where he would go on to become a key cog in the most successful side in the club’s history.



The FA Cup and Conference League winner would lead prayer sessions before training for any members of the squad who wanted to join.

It was not only as a religious leader Lacroix felt comfortable, but in sessions and on the pitch too – comfortable barking at teammates of any standing.



That particular trait will be music to the ears of Alonso and Blues fans, who recognised a squad in desperate need of character and a stronger mentality.

Speaking on the way to lifting the FA Cup with the Eagles in 2025, Lacroix said of his role as a leader: “I’ve always been a leader on and off the pitch, so it’s not really difficult for me.

“But here in this type of locker room you have to show more because everyone has such a big personality and I can show it more here and I like it.”

Lacroix takes standards seriously, but also his own development.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In London, the Frenchman hired his own personal coach who helped him plan his extra workout sessions, his eating habits and even his sleep.

On top of that pursuit of fine margins, he would sit down with the coach and study whichever striker he was going to come up against in the next match to find an edge.

That extra work has helped turn him into one of the best one-on-one defenders in the top flight over the past couple of seasons.



Lacroix offers a blend of Premier League experience while also still having time to develop, a signing to keep all areas of Chelsea happy and similar to the Morgan Rogers deal, which made him the most expensive British player ever.

He brings valuable pace and passion for defending on the front foot.

It is also a clear sign that new boss Alonso will push to implement the back three system which drove his Bayer Leverkusen side to the German title without losing a single game.

The pending addition of Lacroix, who flourished at the heart of Glasner’s back three for Crystal Palace, and wing-back Marco Palestra both point in the same direction.

Some defenders will depart the Blues to make space, but Lacroix will be confident of a starting spot alongside Levi Colwill, who missed almost all of last season through injury.

Alonso will have to wait a while to see Lacroix in action, with the defender now due to return to his holiday having reached the World Cup semi-finals with France.

But once he reports to Cobham, Chelsea will get a taste of an infectious character.

Sports.title: Mason Mount backs Andrey Santos to step into Casemiro’s shoes as Man Utd rethink transfer plans
Sports.content:
MASON MOUNT has taken Andrey Santos under his wing at Manchester United, raving about how quickly his fellow ex-Chelsea star has hit the ground running.

Mount joined forces with £48m newcomer Santos in a deeper pivot for the second time in six days, pulling the strings in a five-goal Rosenborg thrashing.



Afterwards, the former Chelsea captain backed Santos, 22, to fill the void left by Casemiro following the Brazilian veteran’s exit at the end of his contract.

Mount has endured an up and down time at Old Trafford amid injuries, but he believes Santos can flourish as they look to solve the Casemiro void and cover Manuel Ugarte‘s injury.



Mount, 27, said: “Andrey is a really good player. He reads the game brilliantly.

“I know he’s young, but he’s very experienced in going out on loan and playing in the Premier League as well.



“We’re both players that want to get around it, want to put tackles in and win the ball back and be aggressive.

“I’ve really enjoyed it. It’s a position that I love and that I see myself in.”

Santos has been United’s No6 in the first two pre-season games, and while he can clearly play in the position, he lacks ‘marquee’ experience after 13 Prem starts last season.

Meanwhile, Mount made his name higher up the pitch, ex-midfielder Carrick is reimagining him as a fluid No8—reviving the tactical blueprint Erik ten Hag saw wrecked by injury hell.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The pair are throwing down the gauntlet for the opening-day clash against Hull, leaving United’s returning World Cup players with competition.

Mount added: “Defensively we’re both players that want to get around it, want to put tackles in and win the ball back and be aggressive.

“I’ve known Andrey for a while. I’ve watched him from afar, since he’s broken into the first team at Chelsea.”

The pair were technically Blues teammates for six months in early 2023, though Santos was immediately sent back to Vasco da Gama on loan before Mount sealed his £60m summer move to Old Trafford.



United have not ruled out ending the transfer window without a third midfielder and there is no clear frontrunner in the club’s midfield shortlist.

Instead, Ineos are on the look out for a left-sided player and a forward to compliment Benjamin Sesko, who is recovering from a shin problem.

After dropping £85m on Santos and Tielemans, dropping a fortune on a third midfielder would be a massive shock.

United sources admit they would have to sell players first to fund a £68m swoop for Real Madrid powerhouse Aurelien Tchouameni.

The big question now is whether Mount can stay injury-free and hold his ground in a newly flexible midfield.



Together with Santos, summer arrival Youri Tielemans, and Kobbie Mainoo, United suddenly boast a versatile quartet capable of operating across both the No6 and No8 roles.

The ex-England midfielder has started just 25 Prem games since his £60m switch from Chelsea three years ago.

Mount sees himself as a “leader” after wearing the United armband for the first time in the opening 15 minutes of the second half after Harry Maguire was subbed out.

He said: “I’m definitely one, but you have different types of leaders. You have ones that are very vocal.

“I want to always see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch. I’ve been captain previously so I love the role.



“Especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch, being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and even off the pitch as well.

“It’s a role that I really like and I loved having it (the armband) in the second half.”

Mount made a beeline for 19-year-old Shea Lacey after he scored a silky opener in Norway.

Mount received his first senior England call up aged 19, when he was on loan under Frank Lampard Derby County. The last of his 36 caps came at Qatar 2022.

The Portsmouth-born player, under contract until 2028, was once one of the best midfielders in England before injuries savaged his momentum.



But Mount claims he is feeling fitter than ever before the start of a more hectic season schedule.

He said: “I feel brilliant. I feel really, really good. I finished the season well. At the end of last season, playing a few games and being involved.

“Building on that momentum at the end of last season. It’s been a good break, but I was ready and raring to get back and get training again. Getting back into the flow of it.

“Building up over these last couple of weeks. I feel really good. I feel strong and ready to go. I know we’ve got a few more games left and a few more weeks to really work at stuff.”

Sports.title: Arsenal plot return dates for World Cup stars as one trains at former club
Sports.content:
Arsenal plot return dates for World Cup stars as one trains at former club

Arsenal are preparing to welcome back a host of their World Cup stars, who will return in phases, as they face decisions over the fitness of Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka

View 3 Images Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka were both monitored by England for fitness issues during the World Cup (Image: MB Media/Getty Images)

Arsenal are readying for the return of several of their World Cup stars - but face decisions on how best to manage Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka.

‌



Several of the Gunners' players have been back as they're put through their paces, but the majority of their big-hitters were present at this summer's tournament. Those players are entitled to a minimum of three weeks off after their involvement for their countries.

‌



England stalwart Rice has been managing neural pain in his hamstring for more than six months. He was also hampered by sickness during the World Cup and that meant he was hauled off at half-time during the quarter-final win over Norway.

‌



Saka was held back for much of the tournament by Thomas Tuchel, who claimed he was still playing through the pain barrier following an Achilles injury. The winger himself claimed it was fit and healthy and wanted to play more, but Arsenal will now assess him and his colleague as they seek to get them primed for the season.

Kai Havertz is expected to return in the coming days, reports the Evening Standard, but the versatile forward has been training at his former club Bayer Leverkusen this week in preparation.

Piero Hincapie and Viktor Gyokeres have also had their three weeks of holiday after the World Cup and should return next week. Brazilian duo Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli are also due to be back at the start of next week.

‌



Arsenal will play against Girona in Spain on August 1 and Arteta will have some of his World Cup players back, but the clash will come too soon for the likes of Martin Odegaard. Over the 11 days that follows that game they will face Real Betis, Borussia Dortmund and Como.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke were part of England's squad but were by no means regulars, meaning they will be fresher than some ahead of their return.

‌



Norway were beaten by England was on July 11, meaning Odegaard will be available to train again in the week commencing August 3. Spain duo David Raya and Martin Zubimendi have been celebrating their country's triumph played very little football.

Mikel Merino proved himself to be a huge hit off the bench, scoring late winners against Portugal and Belgium, but his impact role meant his minutes were limited, which will aid him in pre-season.

Sports.title: Arsenal exploring stunning Vinicius Junior transfer as Real Madrid star's move approved
Sports.content:
Arsenal exploring stunning Vinicius Junior transfer as Real Madrid star's move approved

Arsenal want to sign a winger before the summer transfer window closes and Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior has emerged as a shock target amid his uncertain future at the Bernabeu

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior has one year left on his Real Madrid contract (Image: Jewel SAMAD/AFP via Getty Images)

Arsenal are interested in signing Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior in what would be a blockbuster transfer move. The Gunners are exploring a move for Vinicius, 26, whose contract in Madrid expires next summer.

‌



The Brazilian's future is therefore uncertain and he features on Arsenal's shortlist in their attempts to sign a wide forward during the summer transfer window. Gunners boss Mikel Arteta recently missed out on signing Morgan Rogers, who's joined Chelsea in a record-breaking £117million deal.

‌



A bombshell report from the Athletic states that Arsenal would be keen on signing Vinicius if he doesn't sign a new deal with Real. Their interest is at an early stage but the move has been approved at all levels within Arsenal.

‌



Talks between Arsenal and Real haven't taken place, but the La Liga giants could look to cash in on Vinicius rather than risk letting him go on a free transfer in 2027. The report adds that the winger would be due a significant loyalty bonus next season, having been at the Bernabeu for eight years.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear READ MORE :

Vinicius is fresh off starring for Brazil at the World Cup, although he wasn't able to help them go beyond the round of 16. Having started all five of their games, the 26-year-old scored four goals for Carlo Ancelotti's side before they were knocked out by Norway.

‌



Last term, Vinicius and Real went trophyless for the second season in a row, despite him scoring 22 goals across all competitions. Jose Mourinho has taken over in the Spanish capital and there are doubts over how important Vinicius is to his plans.

Arsenal also want to sign a striker this summer, with Julian Alvarez and Ollie Waktins linked. After winning the Premier League title, the Guners' co-chairman, Josh Kroenke, said in May: "When you win something, the sun's still going to come up the next day.

Should Arsenal sign Vinicius Junior? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Vinicius Junior scored four goals for Brazil at this summer's World Cup (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

"You've got to get back to work and there are many teams trying to gain on you, including some historically great ones around the Premier League. We're going to look to strengthen because we know teams around us are going to get better. If you're not trying to continually evolve and improve, you're standing still."

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe 'didn't turn up' to meeting and training before shock Woking exit
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe 'didn't turn up' to meeting and training before shock Woking exit

Jermain Defoe's sudden exit as manager of Woking came as a surprise - and the National League side's director of football has now claimed it was prompted by his no-shows

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe's time at Woking came to a bitter end

Jermain Defoe left his position as Woking manager due to a breakdown in communication and a failure to show up to an important meeting, according to the club's director of football.

‌



Former Premier League striker Defoe lasted just six games in charge of the National League side before his departure was announced on Thursday. The 43-year-old, who was appointed at the end of March, said it was "impossible to continue" in the role.

‌



Defoe and Woking "mutually agreed" to part ways following two pre-season friendlies, but the sudden nature of the split made headlines. The Surrey side's director of football, Jody Brown, took to social media to defend the club's transfer policy on Friday and has now released a lengthy statement.

‌



In it, Brown makes some damning claims about Defoe in an effort to give fans "some kind of clarity." "Success as a player does not always translate into management and leadership," Brown said.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

English gymnast taken to hospital after sickening fall onto his head at Commonwealth Games READ MORE :

“I do not intend to discuss internal matters more than necessary or attribute blame," he added before going into lots detail. Brown says that, after being made aware of "growing concerns," he sought out information from Defoe and his assistant, Paul Bracewell.

‌



Brown explained: "To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season. That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.

“A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and Head of Operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session.

"Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.

‌



View 2 Images Jermain Defoe left Woking after just four months (Image: PA)

"Every football club faces challenges. Players want more game time, improved contracts or transfers. The media team might want better equipment, the medical department more interns, the strength and conditioning staff larger gym space. and the car park attendants may want more coffee. But people do not just fail to turn up.

“The experience has highlighted lessons for both myself and the club, particularly around communication with Jermain and his representatives throughout the four months and six matches he was with us. Throughout that period, the club’s objective remained the same: to support the players and staff and give the project every opportunity to succeed.

‌



“I wish Jermain every success in the future and thank him and his staff for their efforts.”

Defoe has been approached by Mirror Football for comment.

In his own statement published on Thursday, he said: "Unfortunately circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position". He added that he was "extremely proud of the work undertaken" and was "really disappointed the journey has ended so soon."

Article continues below

"My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career," he added.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel sends one-word message after Michael Carrick's Man Utd debut snub
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel sends one-word message after Michael Carrick's Man Utd debut snub

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick included JJ Gabriel in the 25-player squad for their pre-season friendly against Rosenborg, but the 15-year-old forward did not feature

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel remained an unused substitute against Rosenborg (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel sent a simple message of "patience" as the wait to debut for Manchester United goes on. The 15-year-old appeared in line to make his senior bow during their pre-season friendly against Rosenborg on Friday.

‌



Gabriel, however, was an unused substitute in Norway, one of two outfield players who did not feature during the 5-0 win. United's 18-year-old midfielder Jim Thwaites joined him in watching on for the entirety, as did backup goalkeeper Tom Heaton.

‌



Three players have missed out in both matches so far this summer. Chido Obi, Dermot Mee and Thwaites were the odd ones out against Wrexham.

‌



Ex-Man Utd star tipped for bright future by Alex Ferguson speaks out on being clubless READ MORE :

Gabriel only came into the squad as a replacement for Ethan Wheatley, and it was Obi who benefited from the change. Michael Carrick also gave game time to Mee instead of Heaton, having started the former England international in Finland.

The only two players who have made a squad but not featured are Gabriel and Thwaites. However, the latter has previously played for United's first team, coming on as a substitute during a post-season friendly against Hong Kong last year.

But the wait for Gabriel to make his bow continues. The teenager acknowledged as much on social media after the match.

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel shared a photo of his Manchester United kit laid out with the word 'patience'

Posting a photo of United's new away kit laid out in the dressing room, with his surname on the back of the shirt, Gabriel added the caption: "Patience". The previous post shared on his Instagram story showed Ayden Heaven and Patrick Dorgu flanking him during a walk around Trondheim.

Another opportunity for Gabriel to feature could come against Atletico Madrid next weekend. However, it remains to be seen whether he makes the squad again, especially if Wheatley returns.

‌



Benjamin Sesko's eventual recovery from a shin injury will seemingly further limit his chances. Gabriel, however, appears to be in no rush.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

After missing out on the squad against Wrexham, he posted on Instagram: "The longer you wait for something, the more you appreciate it when you get it because anything worth having is worth waiting for."

‌



United have further friendlies in August against Leeds United, Milan and Paris Saint-Germain. However, the next best opportunity to make his debut could come in the League Cup third round.

There will not be a chance to play in the EFL Trophy or National League Cup this season, though. United decided not to enter either, partly because they are back in the UEFA Youth League.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino complaint rejected after Donald Trump World Cup interference
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino complaint rejected after Donald Trump World Cup interference

A human‑rights organisation focused on accountability in sport had lodged a complaint against Gianni Infantino, accusing him of a 'repeated breach of political neutrality rules'

View Image Gianni Infantino had been the subject of a complaint filed by a human rights group (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

A complaint filed by a human rights group to the International Olympic Committee (IOC) against FIFA President Gianni Infantino has been rejected, with an IOC spokesperson confirming the matter falls outside the jurisdiction of its Ethics Commission.

‌



FairSquare had submitted the complaint, accusing Infantino of a 'repeated breach of political neutrality rules.' The group previously lodged a similar complaint with FIFA's Ethics Committee last year, alleging Infantino had publicly expressed support for the actions and policies of US President Donald Trump on multiple occasions.

‌



That complaint was reviewed and ultimately dismissed, and the IOC has now taken the same stance. "The IOC Ethics Commission thoroughly analysed the complaint by FairSquare," the IOC spokesperson said.

‌



Argentina players ripped apart over World Cup chaos as FIFA set to take action READ MORE :

World Cup match-fixing probe sparked after suspicious Spain match READ MORE :

"The IOC Ethics Commission noted that the current complaint, including with regard to the FIFA President, refers only to the IF's decisions on its governance and its management, including its relations with government, and to the IF's implementation of the rules of its sport, which are both outside the scope of application of the IOC Code of Ethics.

"The complaint falls outside the IOC Ethics Commission's jurisdiction. FairSquare has been informed accordingly.

Infantino came under scrutiny during the World Cup after being pictured alongside Donald Trump, a moment FairSquare highlighted prominently in its complaint. During the tournament, Trump was involved in several controversial incidents, adding further weight to the group's concerns.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In last Sunday's final, boos echoed around New York New Jersey Stadium as Trump and Infantino walked onto the pitch for the World Cup trophy presentation ceremony.

The American president also waded into the fallout from Folarin Balogun's red card, asking Infantino to intervene, and calls for the FIFA chief's resignation only grew louder. Balogun should have been automatically banned for the game against Belgium after being sent off in his previous game.

‌



However, after Trump and Andrew Giuliani, executive director of the White House's World Cup task force, spoke to Infantino by phone, the automatic one-match suspension was postponed. FIFA announced that the punishment had been suspended, clearing the co-hosts' leading goalscorer to play - though FIFA have insisted that Infantino had no role in the suspension process.

Trump later celebrated the decision on Truth Social, writing: "Thank you to FIFA for doing what was right and reversing a great injustice."

Sports.title: Arsenal get two green lights to proceed with Julian Alvarez transfer in record-breaking deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal get two green lights to proceed with Julian Alvarez transfer in record-breaking deal

Arsenal have been given hope as they continue their quest to sign Julian Alvarez

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

Arsenal have been given two boosts in their pursuit of Julian Alvarez. The Argentina striker has made it clear he wants to leave Atletico Madrid, with Barcelona and Real Madrid both keen to sign him.

‌



Barca are believed to be his preferred destination but Atletico's reluctance to do business with a La Liga rival has given the Gunners a chance of signing him, potentially as part of a cash-plus-player deal involving Viktor Gyokeres.

‌



Spanish title AS reports that Atletico would be open to negotiating with Arsenal if they submit a "considerable" offer. Without any other player involved, the Gunners would need to smash the British transfer record, currently Liverpool's £125m capture of Alexander Isak last summer.

‌



A deal involving Gyokeres would go down with Atletico fans. According to a poll on the same website, 91 per cent of supporters would back an £85m-plus-Gyokeres deal for Alvarez. Atletico were interested in Gyokeres last summer but couldn't match the Gunners' £63.5m offer, including add-ons, to Sporting CP.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Swede helped Arsenal to the title with 14 league goals, a respectable but not prolific return. The former Coventry ace had his detractors for his alleged lack of influence outside the penalty area, prompting some to wonder whether he should be the Gunners' first-choice number nine long term.

‌



Arsenal's dream XI as Bruno Guimaraes signs and Julian Alvarez swap deal done READ MORE :

Last season, Paul Merson claimed that he wasn't "trusted" by his team-mates. During an appearance on Stick to Football, the Gunners legend suggested players were reluctant to give Gyokeres the ball.

He said: "I watch Gyokeres, Arsenal don't trust him, the players. They never pass to him, you watch him, next time he comes short they go 'No.'"

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres could be used as a makeweight in a deal for Alvarez (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Merson added: "If you watch it, you'd be surprised, then when [Gabriel] Jesus comes on, they keep on giving it him all the time. That's what I see when I watch the game."

Meanwhile, another ex-Gunner, Ray Parlour, would welcome the arrival of Alvarez, but alongside Gyokeres rather than instead of him. Parlour told 10Bet: "I think it's a no-brainer. There aren't a lot of great strikers around.

View 3 Images Alvarez has made it clear he wants to leave Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty)

‌



"I'm sure there'd be a lot of clubs after Alvarez, but he would fit in pretty nicely. He's hard-working, a good finisher and quick.

"He's a little bit different to Gyokeres. Sometimes you can play two up front. Maybe he can drop a little bit deeper at times and run off Gyokeres. That could work. That's the position I think they've really got to look at, centre forward."

Sports.title: Arsenal exploring deal for Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr
Sports.content:
Arsenal are looking into a potential deal for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

At this point there has been no club-to-club contact, but the interest is real. Vinicius Jr is one of a number of forward targets Arsenal are exploring, with Julian Alvarez, Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola also players of interest.

The Brazilian international has entered the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Real could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

The Gunners are aiming to strengthen their left-wing options this summer and the Brazil ace would be a superstar addition.

Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard to Besiktas for £17m earlier this summer and have brought in Christo Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m. However, their alternative option in that area of the pitch, Gabriel Martinelli, scored just one Premier League goal last season.

Image: Vinicius Junior celebrates after scoring for Real Madrid at Man City in the Champions League last season

Vinicius Jr, the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up, is currently on holiday following his exploits for Brazil at the World Cup.

Analysis: Vinicius Jr would be jaw-dropping signing for Arsenal

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"It's well known Arsenal are aiming to strengthen their left-wing options this summer - but a deal for Brazil ace Vinicius Junior would be a jaw-dropping addition.

"Vinicius Jr has one year left on his current Real Madrid contract so this could be the window of opportunity for potential suitors to make their move, as Real try to tie the winger down to a new deal.

"Vinicius Jr's relationship with new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has been in focus.

"However, it is understood the player and head coach have been in touch since an incident last season which saw Vinicius Jr abused by Mourinho's Benfica midfielder Gianluca Prestianni and that the pair were ready to start this new campaign together with a clean slate.

"But with Arsenal's interest being reported, there is now the possibility Vinicius Jnr will be kicking off the 206/27 season in the Premier League.

"It's a thrilling thought for Arsenal fans and neutrals on these shores - but a worrying one for the Gunners' title rivals."

Sports.title: Norris puts upgraded McLaren on top from Hamilton in final practice
Sports.content:
Lando Norris gave McLaren hope of challenging for their first Grand Prix pole position of the season in their upgraded car in Hungary by impressively outpacing Friday pacesetter Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes' title-leading Kimi Antonelli in final practice.

Ferrari had appeared the big favourites for Saturday's qualifying fight after dominating the opening day's practice but, while they remained right in the mix at the front, they were usurped in the final hour of practice running by the reigning world champions.

Norris was second to Hamilton after their respective first laps on soft tyres at the end of the session but the McLaren driver then impressively found more speed on his second flying lap, on which he uncorked a 1:17.939 to pip his Ferrari rival to the top of the timesheet by 0.117s.

After an unusually-difficult Friday, Antonelli was back in the mix at the front too and finished third fastest, 0.129s behind Norris.

But team-mate George Russell continued to struggle and wound up only sixth fastest, 0.6s slower than Norris' impressive time.

Charles Leclerc was 0.3s off the pace in fourth in the second Ferrari, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri a tenth further back in fifth. However, it was a more difficult session for Red Bull, with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar seventh and eighth-fastest respectively.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments throughout the years at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle said: "It's so close, as it always is here. It bodes incredibly well for this afternoon."

The battle to head the midfield looks set to be led by Racing Bulls and Audi, with the former's Liam Lawson taking ninth ahead of the latter's Nico Hulkenberg in 10th.

But 13th-fastest Arvid Lindblad completed just six laps in the other Racing Bulls after a power-unit change in the garage kept the British rookie sidelined for all but the session's final minutes.

Cadillac also ran in to problems as a brake fire caused Sergio Perez to pull up in the run-off area at Turn One on his lap out of the pits. The Mexican was unable to return over the rest of the session.

But there was a track return for Lance Stroll in the massively-upgraded Aston Martin after he missed Friday's second session due to the rear-suspension failure that spun him off track in opening practice.

The further encouragement for the Adrian Newey-led team was that the new-look AMR26, which has spent much of the season so far rooted to the back of the grid, outpaced the Williams and Cadillac cars to take 17th for Fernando Alonso and 18th for Stroll in a best time 2.4s off the ultimate pace.

Sports.title: Fury vs AJ moves step closer to being in USA over UK
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's long-awaited heavyweight showdown looks increasingly likely to be in America rather than the UK.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has revealed that Turki Alalshikh, who is organising the all-British bout, now prefers the clash to be in the USA.

Alalshikh previously said that he wants the fight to take place at a time that works for a global audience and would hold talks with the Mayor of London, Sir Sadiq Khan, over a later-than-usual start time.

However, Sky Sports News revealed earlier in the week that Brent Council are yet to be contacted about extending the curfew at Wembley Stadium to allow a 2am ring walk.

Speaking to DAZN ahead of Joshua's warm-up fight with Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia on Saturday, Hearn said: "We've been told in the last 24 hours that [a fight in America] is what they want.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dev Sahni reveals how Tyson Fury toppled Mariusz Wach in a non-TV fight in Thailand and answers two key questions following the heavyweight bout

"That doesn't tally up with the contract that we signed. Until we're happy, we expect every point of that contract to be followed. I feel like this fight should be taking place in the UK.

"Anthony Joshua insisted that the contract stated that the fight must be in the UK.

"If they want to change the contract, then we have to renegotiate the contract. Which, by the way, is not a problem. But it's a conversation we have to have."

Fury: I got through my test, what about AJ?

Fury remains unconvinced that Joshua will agree to the fight and questioned whether his rival has the "guts" to face him.

The 37-year-old, speaking after his seventh-round stoppage of Mariusz Wach in a non-televised bout in Thailand on Friday, referenced Joshua opting not to get in the ring with him after his victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

Image: Fury stopped Wach in the seventh round

Fury said: "I got through my test. Let's see if [Joshua] gets through his test. The biggest test of it all is how big his balls are. I think he's a big s***house.

"In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me. Let's see if he ever does. I'm not convinced.

"I'll regroup. Hopefully the next big fight is signed next week, and we head wherever we're going to head.

"Is it gonna be in Vegas? Is it gonna be in New York? Is it gonna be in Ireland? Is it gonna be in London? Who knows, Belfast maybe? It might even be here in Pattaya, Thailand!"

Sports.title: 'People do not just fail to turn up' - Woking hit back at Defoe after exit
Sports.content:
Woking's director of football Jody Brown claims Jermain Defoe didn't turn up for a meeting and training amid "growing concerns" within the club before he left his role as head coach after just four months.

Defoe had his contract at the National League side mutually terminated on Thursday, having only begun his first managerial role in March, winning two and losing one of his six matches in charge.

The former Tottenham and England striker said that circumstances had made it "impossible for me to continue" and described the job as an "eye-opening" experience.

But in an extraordinary statement on Saturday morning, Woking's Brown hit back at Defoe, saying "success as a player does not always translate into management and leadership" and that there were "growing concerns" within the club during pre-season.

Brown believes Woking were "fully committed" to supporting Defoe and said recruitment, staffing decisions and football matters were "heavily influenced" by the 43-year-old.

"The recommendation to appoint Jermain as manager was mine, and I take full responsibility for it," Brown said. "After meeting with him on several occasions, I believed he was the right person to lead the club into an exciting new era.

"As we have seen many times before, success as a player does not always translate into management and leadership. I sincerely hope to see him succeed in whichever direction he follows."

Brown also revealed a contributing factor to Defoe's shock departure.

He said: "Jermain's feedback was always positive, and he regularly expressed his enthusiasm and excitement for the season, both publicly and privately. I can therefore appreciate the surprise and subsequent speculation surrounding his sudden departure.

"However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns. To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul (Bracewell, assistant) for a brief report outlining the squad's current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season. That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.

"A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and head of operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day's training session. Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.

"Every football club faces challenges. Players want more game time, improved contracts or transfers. The media team might want better equipment, the medical department more interns, the strength and conditioning staff larger gym space. and the car park attendants may want more coffee. But people do not just fail to turn up."

Sky Sports News has contacted Defoe for comment.

Defoe had earlier revealed his decision to leave Woking in a post on Instagram. He wrote: "Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC.

"Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

"I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

"I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club. I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for. The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

"I'm really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

"My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career."

Defoe's six games in charge of Woking 03/04/2026: Woking 3-3 Eastleigh

06/04/2026: Braintree Town 0-0 Woking

11/04/2026: Woking 5-1 Morecambe

14/04/2026: Woking 0-0 Solhull Moors

18/04/2026: Gateshead 0-3 Woking

25/04/2026: Woking 0-1 Halifax Town

What next for Defoe's management career?

Sky Sports' David Richardson:

Defoe had to wait patiently for his first managerial role after coaching jobs at Rangers and Tottenham, jumping in at a level much lower than where he spent his playing career.

Aside from his lack of managerial and non-League experience, the Woking job is far from easy. The club does not have a top budget compared to other National League sides, nor can they fall back on an EFL infrastructure, but that did not deter him. He knew the risks of the role.

"If you speak to any manager, regardless of the league and the standard, it's always going to be a gamble," he said at his unveiling.

"People talk about it being impossible," Defoe had said of ending Woking's wait to reach the Football League. "That means nothing. I truly believe that we can do something special. When you become a manager and a coach, you want that sort of challenge. You want to get up in the morning and have a goal to strive to."

Sky Sports had been in attendance for Defoe's first two games - a six-goal thriller against Eastleigh and a 0-0 draw with Braintree Town. It was a promising start with room for improvement.

The six games at the end of last season gave Defoe a taste of management and, importantly, a chance to put foundations in place. The club did the majority of their transfer business early, making eight new signings to date. He had spoken publicly of his excitement ahead of his first season.

But Defoe's shock departure two weeks before it starts and the public falling-out with Woking will likely damage his future prospects. How keen will other clubs be to take a risk on an unproven manager whose professionalism was called into question during his first role?

Defoe is back to square one and with a reputation to rebuild.

'We'll be fine' - Defoe's final Woking interview

Defoe was upbeat after what proved to be his final game in charge, a 1-0 defeat to Braintree Town in pre-season on Tuesday.

"We're trying to create that elite mentality," he said. "Even in the in-house game the other day, there were a few players that were disappointed that they lost against their friends.

"I stand back and look at it and think that's what you want. You want those sort of demands. It's important to put those sort of demands on the players. It doesn't matter who we play against. We believe that we're good enough to win every game. You have to think like that.

"It's a good group. I'm lucky to have good people in the building, really good players and people that are willing to learn and get better. They're coachable; I think that's important also. We'll be fine. When you've got good players and good people, you're always going to be fine."

Sports.title: Price: People make it too easy for Littler
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price insists he can thwart Luke Littler's bid for back-to-back World Matchplay titles and believes some players ‘make it too easy’ for the defending champion.

Price booked his first World Matchplay semi-final since 2022 with a 16-12 win over Ross Smith at the Winter Gardens, where the 'Ice Man' fired a 102.78 average and closed out victory with a four-leg burst.

The Welshman faces world No 3 Gian van Veen in the last four, with the winner of that semi-final progressing to face either Littler or Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode in Sunday's best-of-35 leg final.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gerwyn Price produced a series of stunning checkouts to beat a testing Ross Smith and book his place in the last four

Littler defeated Price in every Premier League fixture between them this season and a final-set decider in the World Masters semi-finals, while 'The Nuke' remains unbeaten in PDC major matches over 20 legs since his 2024 World Championship final loss.

The world No 1 remains overwhelming favourite to become the first player since Michael van Gerwen to defend his World Matchplay crown, having posted a 109.57 average in his win over Josh Rock, although Price insists he can be stopped.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler admits he's playing some of the best darts of his career after a dominant World Matchplay quarter-final win over Josh Rock

"I think there's a lot of players that can get to that [Littler's] level," Price told reporters after his quarter-final win.

"Is there anyone who can do it as long as him? I think I can and I think there's a couple of players, but he's ruthless at the minute - these 109, 110 averages just look so easy for him.

"I think some players play into his hand and just let him play with his rhythm. It's horses for courses, and sometimes you have to play your game, you have to play the game and you have to play the moments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the quarter-final between Luke Littler and Josh Rock at the World Matchplay

"Sometimes, people make it a little bit too easy for him."

More to come in Van Veen showdown?

Price built a commanding 12-8 lead over Smith in a quarter-final where he threatened to pull further ahead, then found himself level at 12-12 until finishing strongly to reach the last four.

Image: Gerwyn Price, World Matchplay Darts 2026

"I was delighted with the way I played the majority of the game, but there's a couple of legs that I let slip and could have come back to haunt me in the end," Price added.

"I'm thinking I should be 13-7 or 14-6 or whatever it is, because I did waste opportunities and probably shouldn't think like that. I'm just happy to get a win, but frustrated a little bit."

Van Veen admitted he needs to improve after his quarter-final victory over 16-13 James Wade, where he posted a 93 average and also blew a four-leg advantage before closing out victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gian van Veen fires in a magnificent 160 checkout to pull away from James Wade to take a 9-6 lead during their quarter-final

"It felt very poor!" Van Veen admitted to Sky Sports. "My scoring was so terrible. I was so lucky James wasn't scoring as well and my finishing got me through. A win is a win.

"The 118 finish - I really needed it. It was a tight battle but I'm glad I got the job done. Hopefully tomorrow I will be a lot better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gian van Veen edges past James Wade sealing the tie 16-13 and sets up a tantalising World Matchplay semi-final against Gerwyn Price

What's next?

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens on Saturday, with the two semi-finals being played over the best-of-33 to decide who progresses through to Sunday's best-of-35 final.

Defending champion Littler continues his bid for back-to-back titles when he faces Van Duijvenbode, through to the last four at this event for the first time, with Price playing Van Veen in the opening semi-final.

Who will win this year's World Matchplay Darts? Watch throughout the weekend live on Sky Sports. Live coverage continues Saturday from 7.30pm on Sky Sports Action and around 9pm on Sky Sports Main Event. Stream darts and more top sport with NOW.
